# What can be ingested

Three tables. The first is what `POST /ingest` accepts as an entry point, the second is
what the bytes may be, the third is what an optional dependency buys. `GET /capabilities`
answers all three for a running appliance.

## Entry points

A `usetype` names where the content comes from, not what format it is. `probe` measures
the format from the bytes; a usetype only says whether this request carries the content,
a URL, an arXiv id or a local path.

| usetype | content comes from | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `conversation` | `content` | Conversation ingestion: parse JSONL/messages, chunk by turn, embed, optionally RAPTOR + fact extraction |
| `markdown` | `content` | Markdown ingestion: structural split on headings, chunk sections, embed, optionally RAPTOR + fact extraction |
| `raw` | `content` | Raw text ingestion: sentence chunk, embed, optionally RAPTOR + fact extraction |
| `transcript` | `content` | Voice transcript ingestion: sentence chunk with transcript metadata, embed, optionally RAPTOR + fact extraction |
| `wiki:url` | `url` | Fetch a URL, convert HTML→markdown, then run markdown pipeline. |
| `wiki:arxiv` | `arxiv` | Fetch an arXiv paper (metadata + PDF), convert to markdown. |
| `wiki:pdf` | `path` | Convert a local PDF (file path) to markdown. |

## Formats

*Identified from the bytes* means `detect_format` names the format from a signature or an
archive manifest. Anything else is still accepted: the format falls back to the filename
extension, and the file node records that the evidence was a hint rather than a
measurement.

*Can be looked inside* means a prober can measure this format's structural patterns. A
format without one gets an empty pattern set, and every rung guarded on a pattern stands
down — which is the correct outcome, and it is recorded as such rather than assumed.

| format | identified from the bytes | can be looked inside |
|---|---|---|
| `docx` | yes | yes |
| `epub` | yes | no |
| `gif` | yes | no |
| `jpeg` | yes | no |
| `ole2` | yes | yes |
| `pdf` | yes | yes |
| `png` | yes | no |
| `postscript` | yes | no |
| `pptx` | yes | yes |
| `rtf` | yes | no |
| `text` | yes | yes |
| `xlsx` | yes | yes |
| `zip` | yes | no |

## Optional dependencies

A base install carries none of these. Probing an office file needs none of them either;
opening one needs `office`.

| extra | install | what it unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `embed` | `pip install 'jmfts[embed]'` | produce embeddings in this process (torch + sentence-transformers) |
| `office` | `pip install 'jmfts[office]'` | open .docx/.pptx/.xlsx and extract their content; probing them works without it |
| `rdf` | `pip install 'jmfts[rdf]'` | Turtle in, Turtle out, SHACL shapes |
| `sketch` | `pip install 'jmfts[sketch]'` | MinHash per column, for propose:links |
| `convert` | `pip install 'jmfts[convert]'` | drive a LibreOffice worker; the worker itself is a separate image |
